typical_symptoms: Leaf blades rolled longitudinally into trumpet or cone-shaped tubes
Silken threads or webbing binding leaf edges together
Chewed leaf margins and skeletonized leaf tissue within rolls
Presence of small dark fecal pellets (frass) inside or near leaf folds
Yellowing, wilting, and eventual browning/drying of rolled leaves
visual_characteristics: Tubular, cylinder, or funnel-like rolling of individual leaf lobes
Fine white silk threads visible holding the leaf margins intact in a fold
Dark brown to black granular frass specks adhering to the leaf surface
Ragged holes and chewed, necrotic edges along the rolled leaf blade
lesion_characteristics: Irregular chewed leaf margins without defined chlorotic halos
Necrotic dry brown patches where tissue is consumed
Mechanical damage borders following leaf veins or chewed margins
color_characteristics: Healthy green transitioning to pale yellow-green on folded leaf sections
Dark brown to black frass droppings
Dry, reddish-brown to dark brown necrotic tissue at chewed edges
spatial_patterns: Localized tubular folds on individual leaves
Scattered affected leaves throughout upper and middle plant canopy
Irregular feeding patches concealed within leaf rolls
distinguishing_features: Physical rolling/folding of leaf edges secured with silken webbing
Presence of dark granular frass inside the roll
Distinguishable from viral curling by physical binding and feeding damage
